questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was looking for a place where i would feel comfortable, not too different from home but still a change of scenery. Furthermore i wanted to develop my language skills so i was looking for a place where i already knew the basics at least.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I can only recommend to go, it was an incredible experience!!!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was ok. In the beginning i was a bit confused since i had some last minute problems with my registration and
courses..But
i think that overall it was ok, i received some emails upon arrival with the information that i needed to start at the uni.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: You could write to the mobility office at the university. It seemed like there was only one guy dealing with all the problems, which meant it took a while, but he was very helpfull.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Great but slow

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was so much harder than i anticipated. I wanted to find something while i was there, i ended up staying at a hostel for the first month before finding something. In the end i found it on a page called Housinganywhere, it was expensive but a nice location!
I would actually do it the same way again since i thought it was nice to get a feel for the city before choosing where i wanted to live. And i also met some amazing people at the hostel who were in the same situation as me!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think it was really nice. The university is split up over the whole city, but it's very well connected by public transportation. Not living in the student housing meant that i could easily invite friends over or host my friends who visited e from home, which was really nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very simple, you just had to choose the courses that you wanted on the unimia page. They sent instructions on how.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: once again i think you could write the mobility office, but it wasn't necessary since it was very simple.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that i wanted without any problems.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can change your courses even after they begin, this makes it possible to try them out and see what you like. And you have to register for exams yourself, this was probably the hardest. not because it was complicated, but because the registration is only open for a few weeks.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took masters classes at the university even though i am a bachelor student. In 3/5 of the courses the level was lower than what i am used to at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The lectures were more interactive. The exams were without any type of help (no books, notes or anything)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ADVANCED INDUSTRIAL ORGANIZATION (6)
FINTECH INDUSTRY (6)
DECISION THEORY AND BEHAVIOURAL ECONOMICS (6)
PORTFOLIO OPTIMIZATION (6)
GLOBAL FIRMS AND MARKETS (6)
I also took the italian course that they have, this gives 3 credits if its on level A2 or above.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really enjoyed the decision theory and behavioural economics course, since it combined some thing i knew fro economics with some psychology. 
I also liked the fintech course, the professor was not my favourite, but the topic was really interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't think that i needed to get a sim-card but luckily it wasn't too expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was actually more expensive than i thought it would be. The sim-card was less expensive than i thought. And housing was more expensive than i thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You could join a lot of stuff. The people from ESN arranged all sorts of things! anything from volleyball to escape rooms and wine nights. There was even a ski trip that you could go on. The possibilities were endless.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I went to the intro night which was a bit overwhelming, but a nice way to get an introduction to the ESN. I also recommend going to the karaoke night. It was a lot of fun!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I went to a lot of the cities around Milan while i was there. Milan is really well connected so this was a great opportunity to explore. I went to Monza, Bergamo, Bologna, Venice and Como. I also went on a one day ski trip with some friends in Valmalenco. There are a lot of beautiful museums in Milan too. Otherwise i recommend going to the markets that are all around town, here you can buy anything from clothes to vegetables and practise your italian ;-)
And of course have aperitivo and go out with your friends, the nightlife in Milan is good!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was easy since i have been in italy many times before, so nothing was completely new to me.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: People are so nice and open! I found that they always invite you to join them for whatever they are doing and that they are really good at including the erasmus students in the things that are happening outside of class as well. I met some italians at the hostel where i stayed in the beginning and then in class at uni and they are honestly amazing. I worked in a group with them in school so it came pretty naturally, but im sure if you just introduce yourself they will be happy to talk to you!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They are late for everything (at least my friends..)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The going out! You go out to have a coffee, you go out to study, you go out to have aperitivo, you go out to enjoy the sun, to have a gelato, to eat dinner, the list goes on...
And then the openness, i really want to adopt their thing of inviting people everywhere i think it's so nice!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: They don't turn on the heating until 15. of October so it gets a bit cold there for a few weeks. Bring sunscreen it's sunny 4/5 days. Enjoy it while you can, it flys by!!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The classes at the economics department is in trimesters. This meant that i had to do a semesters worth of classes in just a trimester. However you can do the exams many times, so i just chose to do half in december when my classes ended and the other half in January were i had more time.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting the best people, improving my italian and getting to know another city so well!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was difficult being away from my family but luckily we have facetime!! I think the exam periods were the greatest challenge. You go from having so much fun everyday to just sitting in your room and reading day in and day out and being stressed by the exams, not so fun...

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
